I'm cursed with a blessing,

an over active mind with a very intense imagination,

I am not neat,

my room is a metaphor for my life,

everything every where and I only I know where it is and where it goes.

I can weigh the likelihoods but that doesn't stop me from being scared.

I can see the chances and picture the differences

that doesn't mean they can't sit right in front of me every waking hour.

I can't shut my brain off,

my brain is driven by some kind of fuel that is always at full tilt until it crashes.

The energy it needs to kill itself is supplied by itself.

No amount of relaxation can settle this.

No amount of tears can release this.

No amount of anything can stop this.

I can only make it relax for a brief while.

I can lie and lie and lie to myself,

the phrase, "there is always tomorrow." is seldom not said.

I don't.

push button.

one for me and the other for the things I want to think.

being able to think quickly just means I'm able to scare myself faster.

No thinking.

No thinking.

to throw everything to the wind and not worry about tomorrow.

Because my over active blessing will take me to a world where all is over.

My life in taters because I made a few dumb mistakes,

I made teenage mistakes,

but yet, that's all it takes.

I'm rolled up paranoia, with a dollop of anxiety.

An over active eater and thinker with a frightening mind.

I am cursed with no blessing.

I visited cnn.com at around 6pm today and there was a new subsection related to WAR. right on the homepage, there was a section for "military matters" with several very aggressively worded articles relating to the military (surprise).

The main article claims to document an active reconnaissance mission aboard an active duty navy spy plane, but ends with a CNN anchor wondering if, in a nutshell, the confrontations with China will become much more physical in the near future. China article

This subsection of CNN was right on the homepage for a few minutes, right up until I refreshed my screen. I can't help but feel that they are actively preparing us for some kind of major conflict by making this type of discussion a central part of the national dialogue. I wouldn't have thought twice if they didn't remove it from the homepage so quickly, I have a background in marketing/market research and this is the type of tactic we use to analyze whether or not a topic has staying power and can influence key opinion leaders.
